rationale: The workflow already implements the cancel-superseded-runs optimization via `concurrency: group: "pages", cancel-in-progress: true`, which cancels an in-progress deployment when a newer revision starts on the same concurrency group (pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE; preconditions met: same workflow/branch, newer run supersedes older checks). No other pattern's preconditions are satisfied: there is no dependency-installation step to cache (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE), no matrix to fail-fast (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST), no scheduled workflow to pause or suppress (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE), no test suite to prioritize/select (P-LIT-PRIORITIZE, P-LIT-SELECT), no Bazel build (P-LIT-BAZEL-*), and no evidence of runaway jobs warranting a custom timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT). Path filtering (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER) is not safe here because shared configuration or the `./web/build.sh` generator could depend on files outside `web/`, and this is a deployment workflow where required-status semantics must be preserved. Skipping runs (P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW) is behavior-changing and unsupported without an approved skip policy. The observed CI history shows short, successful runs (~17-36s), so there is no demonstrated waste to remove. Adding any change would be unrelated or risk weakening deployment coverage.
